scope:
Package K1c-1 (kernel + words): the owner sees TWO different numbers for the SAME widened request. After tapping 'Szerzej' the composer menu / sheet says 'Szacunek: nastepne zapytanie bedzie ok. 1.1x zwyklego', and after sending, the receipt's 'straznik x10' shows 1.8x of the base for that very request. Two numbers with different bases that contradict each other are exactly what the owner wants gone (everything shown must be true and say what it is measured against). Branch claude/m1-w0 is at 51684e78 (= main; W1c is in, wording of the ratio is data-driven: 'nieznane - brak bazy' / 'duzo mniej niz zwykle' / one decimal from 0.1). Read docs/reports/QUEUE_S1.md section 'DOC1 GOTOWE' (the 'Znalezisko do wyjasnienia (K1c)' paragraph) and nothing else of it.
STEP 1 - MEASURE, do not guess. Candidate causes to check one by one with a small kernel test or a one-off probe (record the numbers in your card): (a) the pre-send estimate is compiled by ChatEngine::context_guard (loom/src/chat/chat_engine.cpp ~line 1010) called from loom/src/actions/ops.cpp ~line 2337 (context.modify) with text "" and a default ChatOptions probe, while the real send compiles with the user's text, attachments and the options of the send (model, stream, reasoning recipe) - find every difference between the two compilations; (b) the baseline: request_guard (chat_engine.cpp ~line 91) reads the usage ledger baseline by usage_baseline_key(cfg,'chat.send',endpoint,model) - check that the estimate and the send read the SAME baseline at the same moment (a send in between enters the ledger and moves it; the first send after 'Szerzej' may be compared with a base that already contains the widened request); (c) which field the web shows as 'ok. N x zwyklego' (loom/web/src/components/context-receipt-state.ts ratioText, use-context-modify.ts, composer-menu.ts, ContextSlider.tsx) - guard.ratio, growth_factor, or bytes divided by something else - and which field the receipt sheet shows. STEP 2 - DECIDE (technical decisions are yours, R1-R53: everything configurable, defaults are presets, no invented limits; write the decision and how to reverse it into docs/reports/INDEX.md under 'S1 / M1-K1c1'). Preferred: both numbers answer the same question with the same base - the estimate is compiled the way the send will compile it (give context.modify and the probe an optional pending text/options so the composer can pass what the user typed; when none is passed say in words that the estimate is for an empty message) and is compared with the same baseline the send will use. If two bases are legitimately different, name each base in words next to the number in BOTH places (pack words, pl + en, e.g. 'wzgledem zwyklego zapytania w tej rozmowie'), never an unlabeled 'x'. Do NOT change the x10 rule (UsagePolicy decides; only a x10 jump is asked), do NOT regenerate or edit loom/tests/fixtures/golden/chat_request_legacy.json, do not change the receipt schema loom.context_receipt/1 incompatibly (additive fields only; if you add a field, update the docs of the receipt and the compat tests). STEP 3 - TESTS: a kernel test (doctest, loom/tests/, one file per area - extend test_context_receipt.cpp or the K1b test that already compiles estimate and send) proving that for the same widened request the estimate before and the receipt guard after agree (tolerance only where the text length differs by construction, stated in the test) and that a send between them does not silently change the meaning of the base; web unit tests for any new words (test:context-receipt / test:composer-menu). If you add a web API route literal run the registry chain (python3 loom/tools/gen_graph_interfaces.py -> python3 loom/src/model/gen_runtime_profiles.py (then --check) -> re-pin the sha256 of graph/interfaces.pack in loom/data/data_domains.pack -> ctest -R 'graph_entry|kb_pack|kb_data_domains|runtime_profile|onboarding_pack|graph_proj'); if not, say 'no new route literal'. Words live in loom/data/profiles/conversation_view.pack (regenerate loom/src/onboarding/builtin.inc and loom/web/src/onboarding/generated/conversation-view.json with gen_onboarding_pack.py - it emits explicit chunk lengths, keep that; then python3 tools/clang_inc_check.py loom/build/dev must stay all ok). Commit in 2-3 pieces (measure+test -> kernel -> words/web) and push to origin claude/m1-w0. If after about 50 tool calls a piece is unfinished, commit what is consistent and return done=false with exactly what is left.
accept: cmake --build --preset dev (once per change, in the background, polled with short calls) succeeds; ctest --preset dev -R 'context_receipt|context_modify|chat_request|context_data|onboarding_pack|kb_pack|settings_fields|graph_entry' green (and test_abi_compat if loom.h changed - it should not); cd loom/web && npm run build and npm run test:context-receipt, test:composer-menu, test:context-strip pass; python3 loom/src/onboarding/gen_onboarding_pack.py --check clean; python3 tools/clang_inc_check.py loom/build/dev all ok; node e2e/m1-context-menu-native.mjs and e2e/m1-context-sent-native.mjs pass TWICE in a row with git status clean afterwards (screenshots to a scratch M1_SHOTS_DIR); pushed to origin claude/m1-w0. The card pastes: the measured numbers BEFORE (estimate vs guard for the same widened request, each with its base) and AFTER the change, the cause found (which of a/b/c or other), the rendered texts of the estimate and the guard, the decision with how to reverse it.
rules_extra: Shared machine: never kill processes by name; record the pid/port you started (e2e servers on your own port). Do NOT run the full gate (S1 does). CACHE RULE: no single tool call longer than ~4 minutes - run builds and tests in the background and poll with short calls. One native build at a time (disk is small: no second build tree; use loom/build/dev of this worktree). Keep context small: grep and line ranges, never dump big files. ASAN pitfall: never range-for over .at()/.value()/operator[] of a by-value temporary - bind to a named const first (tools/lint_asan_range_for.py [base] lists suspicious lines). Tests must not depend on speed or order: wait for conditions, never read a UI attribute right after a tap. Private data: tests use synthetic data only; never read docs/exports or eval/real-holdout-key. Texts for the owner in plain Polish and English; nothing described as working that is only planned. Do not touch loom/android/smoke/* (owned by the parallel session).
